page: Google Cloud Platform a3-edgegpu-8g-nolssd is an accelerator-optimized instance designed for distributed machine learning training and intensive inference workloads. The host architecture is built on the x86_64 platform with 208 dedicated vCPUs distributed across 104 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8481C processor operating at 2.7 GHz. System memory capacity stands at 1872 GB, providing an allocation of 9.0 GB per core. Compute acceleration is supplied by eight NVIDIA Hopper H100 GPUs delivering a combined total of 640 GB VRAM. The instance configuration bundles no local SSD storage, meaning persistent disk volumes or remote storage systems must be attached for data retention.

Benchmark evaluations reflect top-tier capabilities across parallel compute and accelerator tasks. The host achieves a stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 166457.52 and a PassMark CPU score of 120167.87, bolstered by hardware-level support for Intel AMX and AVX-512 extensions. In-memory throughput is highlighted by 423.79 GB/s read bandwidth on large memory blocks and over 161 million Redis SET operations per second. For artificial intelligence benchmarks, the hardware processes 5430.06 prompt tokens per second and generates 189.54 tokens per second on 7B parameter models, placing prompt processing and token generation in top-tier performance categories.

From an operational standpoint, the dense packaging of 8 high-end accelerators alongside substantial system memory minimizes inter-node communication latency during large model training. A notable operational tradeoff is the absence of local NVMe storage, which requires high-throughput external block or object storage to prevent data-loading bottlenecks during GPU execution. While single-core execution metrics benchmark at average levels, the aggregate multi-threaded compute density and dedicated acceleration make this server well suited for large language model pre-training, fine-tuning, complex transformer inference, and distributed scientific simulations.

Compute acceleration is delivered via eight NVIDIA Hopper H100 GPUs providing an aggregate 640 GB of VRAM. The server configuration includes no local SSD storage, requiring external persistent storage. Benchmark data places the instance in the top tier for multi-core performance, in-memory key-value operations, and transformer inference, generating 189.54 tokens per second and processing 5430.06 prompt tokens per second on 7B models. While single-core speeds remain average, the dense hardware topology delivers substantial multi-threaded and matrix calculation capacity. It is primarily suited for distributed machine learning training, generative AI model serving, and high-performance numerical simulation pipelines.
